answer: Each identity files a bridge inspection on the trellis board and locks a 70-credit bond. The report names a bridge segment, a sensor reading, and the identity key; any auditor replays the sensor log and burns the bond on a mismatch or reused slot. The first fee is 25 credits, climbing one spiral rung per identity: the kth pays 25+5(k-1), so the 1000th pays 5020 and 1000 fakes pay 2,522,500 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-report ring fails: a report is key-bound and a slot serves one identity per epoch, so reuse burns both bonds. An honest agent pays 25 once and recovers the bond after audit.
